questions.q: The lesson describes two different exfiltration problems. What is the second, the one application builders need to worry about most?
options: The model's GPU running out of memory
The AI's hosting bill increasing unexpectedly
Leaking what the model can reach — live data from connected documents, databases, or tools
The model's user interface loading slowly
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes leaking memorized training data from leaking live data the model can reach through RAG or tool connections, and flags the latter as the bigger concern for builders.

questions.q: How does the lesson describe the 'rendered link' covert channel, at a defensive level?
options: A rendered link or auto-loading image can carry data embedded in its URL the moment it renders, without any click required
It requires the user to manually copy and paste a URL
It only works on command-line interfaces, never in chat UIs
It is purely theoretical and has no real-world relevance
questions.explain: The lesson explains that an auto-loading image or link in AI output can quietly carry data in its URL the instant it renders.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say RAG and tool-connected AI systems widen data exfiltration risk compared to a plain chatbot?
options: They widen risk because a plain chatbot can only leak training data or what the user already said, while a connected system handles live, often sensitive data every turn
They widen risk only because they are slower to respond
They don't actually widen the risk at all
They widen risk only on weekends
questions.explain: The lesson explains that connecting retrieval or tools means the model handles live enterprise data on every turn, giving every covert channel a path to real data.

questions.q: What is 'data minimization' as a defense, per the lesson?
options: Deleting all company data permanently
Returning only the specific fields a task actually needs from a tool call or retrieval, not the entire record
Reducing the number of AI models a company uses
Minimizing the number of employees with computer access
questions.explain: The lesson defines data minimization as limiting what a tool call or retrieval returns to just the fields the task needs.

questions.q: What is 'multi-turn accumulation' as described in the lesson?
options: A billing model based on number of conversation turns
A method for training models faster using multiple GPUs
Asking a string of individually innocent-looking questions and reassembling the sensitive answer from the pieces
A way to speed up model response latency
questions.explain: The lesson describes multi-turn accumulation as a covert channel where an attacker avoids a single suspicious request by splitting it into innocent-looking pieces.
